world.setting: Contemporary creative and digital world — artist studios, home offices, open internet, maker spaces, and social platforms of the early 2010s
world.register: Accessible, energetic, maker-culture manifesto; warm and conversational

creator.name: The Creator
creator.look: A creative professional in their 30s — scruffy, approachable, ink-stained hands; wearing a casual hoodie and jeans; the Everyman who makes things and shares them openly

peer.name: The Fellow Maker
peer.look: A fellow artist in her late 20s from the same scene — paint on her sleeves, tote bag of zines, curious and generous; the peer you trade work and notes with

office.look: A creative studio or home office — warm lamp light, bookshelves packed with art books and zines, a cluttered desk with a laptop and scattered sketches, sticky notes everywhere

room.look: A maker's living space — comfortable chaos, art prints on walls, a sketchbook open on a coffee table, phone charging nearby

stage.look: A talk stage or open-mic setting — a creator presenting their work publicly for the first time, warm spotlight, an audience of fellow makers

abstract.look: Abstract digital space representing the open internet — minimal, clean white background with floating text, icons, and connection lines suggesting social sharing and community

street.look: An urban creative neighborhood — gallery storefronts, murals on brick walls, people with portfolios and cameras, coffee shop windows

cafe.look: A neighborhood coffee shop where makers trade notes — laptops, sketchbooks and a community bulletin board

library.look: A cabinet of curiosities / personal library — shelves of influences, books, records and pinned-up clippings the creator curates

classroom.look: A workshop classroom where the creator teaches what they know — whiteboard of process sketches, students with notebooks

kitchen.look: A working kitchen — the chef who shares the recipe; ingredients and process on the counter

objects.why: Daily dispatches, sketchbooks, drafts — the raw process made visible
Posting the daily dispatch; the feed; stock vs flow
Documenting the work in progress, behind the scenes
Teaching and sharing as generosity; open-sourcing the recipe
Influences, the cabinet of curiosities, crediting sources
The finished work is the tip; the process underneath is what people connect with
Selling out vs passing the hat; getting paid for the work
Daily practice, one day at a time, chain-smoking projects
Opening the studio; letting people in

spine.claim: The lone genius myth is a lie — creativity grows in 'sceniuses', communities of makers who share process openly
Documenting your daily process — the sawdust and sketches — is more magnetic than the finished masterpiece
Sharing generously requires courage: teaching trade secrets, opening the cabinet of curiosities, and embracing amateur status
Building an audience means avoiding the trap of becoming 'human spam' — giving more than you take
Process over product: show your work so you find the fellow travelers you were meant to create with
